question: Can the engine be made to name the party that sent a wrong share?

before.message: Fatal error at fp2000-0:3 (MULS): inconsistent Shamir secret sharing
before.note: identical for a different culprit --- the 3 is the instruction offset
before.or_worse: Fatal error in communication: read_some: stream truncated, when the bad data belongs to a party the others reach later, so the obvious attribution points at whichever process exited first

after.message: inconsistent Shamir secret sharing sent by player 0
inconsistent Shamir secret sharing sent by player 1
inconsistent Shamir secret sharing sent by player 3
inconsistent Shamir secret sharing sent by player 5
inconsistent Shamir secret sharing sent by player 6
more than 2 parties sent wrong shares, which is beyond the decoding capacity of this sharing
after.note: correct behaviour. Naming somebody past capacity would be worse.

cost.why: ShamirMC::exchange is a partial broadcast that makes each party a sender to the 2t+1 nearest. Locating needs the whole codeword, so each party goes from four correspondents per opening to six.

what_it_reaches: Rung 2, identifiable abort, and rung 3 or 4 if the shares are published --- the decode is deterministic, so anyone holding the transcript reaches the same verdict. NOT rung 5: naming the party and recovering the opened value does not repair the bad triple underneath it.

predictions.traffic unchanged because POpen_Begin ca: WRONG. That is the unbatched path. The batched one, exchange(), is a partial broadcast and is what runs. Measured 1.50x online. Third time in this project that reading one code path and assuming it is the one that executes has cost a number.
predictions.names the party correctly: landed, five parties and three pairs

still_open: A party that substituted its INPUT. secret_input() sums one additive share per party, so a substituted input is a valid sharing of a different value --- nothing is inconsistent and there is no codeword to decode. That fix is one opening per party instead of one over all inputs, and is not implemented.
